title: Number of Unique Flavors After Sharing K Candies
statement:
The value `candies[i]` is the flavor of candy `i`. You must give your sister exactly `k` candies that sit next to each other in the array (one contiguous block of length `k`) and you keep all the rest.

Pick the block so that the candies you keep cover as many different flavors as possible, and return that number of flavors. When `k` is `0` you keep everything; when `k` equals the array's length you keep nothing.
notes:
## Intuition

The candies you give away always form a window of length `k`, and the window can start at any of `n - k + 1` places. Rebuilding the set of kept flavors for every start costs O(n · k). Instead, count every flavor once, take the first window out, and then slide it: each step takes exactly one candy away and gives exactly one back, so the number of flavors still kept changes by at most two in O(1).

## Approach

1. Count every flavor in `count`; `kept` starts as the number of distinct flavors.
2. Give away the first window, `candies[0..k-1]`: decrement each count, and when a count drops to `0`, that flavor is no longer kept.
3. `best` starts as `kept`.
4. For each `i` from `k` on, the window moves one step right: give away `given = candies[i]` (a count reaching `0` loses a flavor), then take back `back = candies[i - k]` (a count rising from `0` regains one).
5. Update `best` after every step and return it.

Giving away before taking back makes `k = 0` work with no special case: the same candy goes out and straight back in.

## Example 1, step by step

`candies = [1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 3]`, `k = 3`. Counts are `{1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 2, 4: 1}`, so `kept = 4`. Giving away `[1, 2, 2]` empties flavors 1 and 2: `kept = 2`, `best = 2`. At `i = 3`, give a `3` (count 1 left) and take back the `1`: `kept = 3`. At `i = 4`, give the `4` (`kept = 2`) and take back a `2` (`kept = 3`). At `i = 5`, give a `3` (count 0, `kept = 2`) and take back a `2` (count was 1, no change). The answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each candy is counted once, given away at most once and taken back at most once.
- Space: O(m) for `count`, where m is the number of distinct flavors.

## Pitfalls

- A flavor is lost only when its count reaches `0`, not whenever one candy of it is given away.
- When `k` equals the array length the whole array is given away and the answer is `0`.
- Taking back before giving away breaks `k = 0`, because `candies[i - k]` would be a candy that was never given.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | for each flavor, how many candies of it you currently keep |
| `kept` | number of flavors with a count above `0` |
| `best` | most flavors kept over all windows so far |
| `given` | candy that enters the window and goes to your sister |
| `back` | candy that leaves the window and comes back to you |

narration.2: count tracks how many candies of each flavor you keep.
narration.6: Every distinct flavor is kept before anything is given away.
narration.7: Give away the first window, candies 0 to k - 1.
narration.8: One fewer candy of this flavor is kept.
narration.9: If none are left, this flavor is no longer kept.
narration.11: The first window is the best seen so far.
narration.12: Slide the window right one candy at a time.
narration.14: Candy i enters the window, so you keep one fewer of its flavor.
narration.15: Its flavor is lost if that was the last one you had.
narration.16: Candy i - k leaves the window and comes back to you.
narration.17: If you had none of that flavor, you regain it.
narration.18: Add the returned candy to its flavor's count.
narration.19: Remember the most flavors kept for any window.
narration.21: Return the best number of kept flavors.
